mainTopic: Sterilizing remedies and סירוס; healing teeth and loins on שבת (vinegar, rose oil); רבא's retraction because of הוֹאִיל; רב's ruling like רבי שמעון.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a question from the previous page: how may anyone drink a remedy for jaundice that causes sterility, when causing sterility (סירוס) is forbidden? The גמרא proves that sterilizing someone already sterile is still forbidden, so it rejects a סריס and then an old man, and settles on a woman. For רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא, who holds that women are also commanded in פרו ורבו, it must be an old or barren woman. Then a new משנה teaches that on שבת you may not do obvious medical treatment for aching teeth or loins, but you may act in your normal everyday way. רבי שמעון adds that all Jews count as princes, so anyone may use rose oil. The גמרא explains how vinegar can heal teeth when a פסוק says it harms them. Next it settles a clash between the משנה and a ברייתא about sipping vinegar, through the answers of אביי and רבא. It concludes that רבא retracted his own answer because of his principle of הוֹאִיל. Finally, רב rules like רבי שמעון on rose oil, and the גמרא begins a challenge from another teaching of רב that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Leavening a meal-offering that is already leavened
steps.stepSummary: Everyone agrees that leavening a מנחה that someone else already leavened is still a punishable act.
steps.simpleTranslation: Everyone agrees that one who leavens after another person already leavened is liable, as it says 'It shall not be baked leavened' and 'It shall not be made leavened.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a challenge to the earlier answer that the sterilizing remedy is permitted for someone who is already a סריס. It starts by bringing a parallel case about leavening a מנחה, setting up the main attack in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah repeats the ban on חמץ in a מנחה twice. This teaches that every act of leavening counts, even if the dough is already leavened. The same reasoning is about to be applied to סירוס.

keyTerms.meaning: it shall not be baked leavened (ויקרא ו:י)

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not about פסח. It is about leavening a מנחה offering in the בית המקדש.

phrases.english: All agree regarding one who leavens after one who leavened
that he is liable,
as it is said: 'It shall not be baked leavened,'
'It shall not be made leavened.'
phrases.notes: The doubled wording teaches that each separate act of leavening counts on its own.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַכֹּל מוֹדִים בִּמְחַמֵּץ אַחַר מְחַמֵּץ שֶׁהוּא חַיָּיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues from the previous page, where the remedy was permitted for a סריס.
steps.kashyaTarget: The earlier answer that the sterilizing remedy is permitted for someone already sterile.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a second act of leavening is still forbidden, a second act of sterilizing may also be forbidden.

steps.title: Castrating someone already castrated is also forbidden
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק listing four kinds of damage shows that one who sterilizes after another person already sterilized is liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: Similarly, one who castrates after another castrated is liable, as it says 'bruised, crushed, torn, or cut.' If one is liable for 'cut,' then surely for 'torn' (fully detached)! So the extra word comes to include one who detaches after another already cut, and he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its challenge. It proves from a פסוק that sterilizing someone who is already sterile is still forbidden, so the remedy cannot be allowed for a סריס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נתוק (fully detached) is worse than כרות (cut), so it should not need its own mention. The Torah lists it anyway to teach that detaching after cutting is a new punishable act. That knocks down the earlier answer.

keyTerms.meaning: all the more so (a קַל וָחוֹמֶר)

steps.whyThisMatters: It sets the rule that סירוס applies even to someone already sterile, which forces the גמרא to find a new case where the remedy is allowed.

phrases.english: Regarding one who castrates after one who castrated, that he is liable,
as it is said: 'And bruised, and crushed,
and torn, and cut,'
If one is liable for 'cut,'
for 'torn off,' is it not all the more so!
Rather, it comes to include one who detaches after one who cut,
that he is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the leavening parallel to סירוס.
steps.kashyaTarget: Permitting the remedy for a סריס.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The extra word נתוק shows that sterilizing after sterilizing is still forbidden.

steps.title: The remedy is for an old man
steps.stepSummary: New answer: the sterilizing remedy is permitted for an old man who can no longer have children.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is speaking of an old man.
steps.whatsHappening: After the first answer fell, the גמרא suggests a new case. An elderly man who cannot have children anyway would not be harmed by the remedy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that if a man cannot have children at all, there is nothing left to sterilize. The next step will challenge this assumption.

phrases.english: Rather, with an old man.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected סריס answer.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The remedy is for a סריס.
steps.terutzMaskana: The remedy is for an old man who cannot have children.

steps.title: Even old men can regain fertility
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן said certain remedies restored him to youth, so an old man may still be fertile.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רבי יוחנן say: 'These remedies restored me to my youth!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the old-man answer. רבי יוחנן's statement shows that an old man can still become able to have children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If an old man can be made fertile again, sterilizing him still destroys something real. So the old-man answer does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: but didn't he say? (opening a challenge)
they returned me to my youth

phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Yochanan say:
These are what returned me to my youth!
phrases.notes: Referring to remedies that restore fertility.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן הֵן הֵן הֶחְזִירוּנִי לְנַעֲרוּתִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the old-man answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that an old man has no fertility to lose.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An old man can become fertile again, so sterilizing him is still סירוס.

steps.title: The remedy is for a woman
steps.stepSummary: New answer: the remedy is for a woman, who is not commanded in פרו ורבו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is speaking of a woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a third answer. A woman may drink the sterilizing remedy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the main view, a woman is not obligated in פרו ורבו, and the ban of סירוס does not apply to her in the same way. So she may use the remedy.

phrases.english: Rather, with a woman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected old-man answer.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The remedy is for an old man.
steps.terutzMaskana: The remedy is for a woman.

steps.title: According to רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא women are also commanded
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא holds that women are also commanded in פרו ורבו, so how could a woman use the remedy according to him?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא, who says the verse 'God blessed them and said to them, be fruitful and multiply' speaks to both of them, what is there to say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how the woman answer works for the opinion that women are also obligated to have children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'to them,' in the plural, so רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא includes women. For him, a woman sterilizing herself would also be a problem.

keyTerms.meaning: upon both of them (man and woman)
what is there to say? (how would he explain it?)

phrases.english: And according to Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka,
who said: About both of them it says:
'And God blessed them
and said to them: Be fruitful and multiply' —
what is there to say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the woman answer according to a minority opinion.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If women are commanded in פרו ורבו, a woman may not sterilize herself either.

steps.title: An old woman or a barren woman
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא, the remedy is for an elderly woman or a barren woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: With an old woman, or alternatively, with a barren woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the last question. Even רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא would allow the remedy for a woman who cannot have children anyway.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An old man could still be made fertile, as רבי יוחנן said, but an old or barren woman cannot. So here there is nothing to destroy, and the remedy is allowed even for רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא.
steps.whatToRemember: Final result: the sterilizing remedy may not be given to a סריס or an old man. It may be given to a woman, and according to רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא, only to an old or barren woman.

phrases.english: With an old woman,
or alternatively, with a barren woman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any woman may use the remedy.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא, only a woman who cannot conceive may use it.

steps.title: Toothache and vinegar on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that one with a toothache may not sip vinegar as treatment, but may dip food in vinegar normally.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One who has pain in his teeth may not sip vinegar through them, but he may dip his food in his usual way, and if he is healed, he is healed.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins about healing on שבת. Obvious medical treatment is forbidden, but normal eating that happens to heal is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Swishing vinegar on the teeth looks like medicine, which חז״ל forbade on שבת. Dipping bread in vinegar is ordinary eating, so any healing that comes from it is just a side effect.
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets the basic rule for medicine on שבת: actions that look like treatment are forbidden, but normal everyday actions are allowed even if they heal.

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
One who has pain in his teeth —
may not sip vinegar through them,
but he may dip in his usual way,
and if he is healed — he is healed.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַחוֹשֵׁשׁ בְּשִׁינָּיו לֹא יְגַמֵּעַ בָּהֶן אֶת הַחוֹמֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Medicinal sipping is forbidden; normal dipping is allowed even if it heals.

steps.title: Pain in the loins and smearing oils
steps.stepSummary: One with pain in the loins may not smear wine and vinegar, may smear plain oil, but not rose oil, except princes who use it during the week.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who has pain in his loins may not smear wine and vinegar, but he may smear oil, though not rose oil. Princes may smear rose oil on their wounds, since that is their normal way during the week.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a second example of the same rule. Plain oil is normal, but wine, vinegar, and rose oil are treated as medicine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People smear plain oil on themselves all the time, so it does not look like healing. Rose oil is expensive, and ordinary people use it only as medicine. Princes use it every day, so for them it is normal.

phrases.english: One who has pain in his loins —
may not smear wine and vinegar,
but he may smear oil.
But not rose oil.

phrases.aramaic: בְּנֵי מְלָכִים סָכִין שֶׁמֶן וֶרֶד עַל מַכּוֹתֵיהֶן,
phrases.english: Princes may smear rose oil on their wounds,
since it is their way to smear it on weekdays.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַחוֹשֵׁשׁ בְּמׇתְנָיו לָא יָסוּךְ יַיִן וָחוֹמֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second application of the same rule in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Plain oil is permitted; wine, vinegar, and rose oil are forbidden, except for princes who use rose oil normally.

steps.title: All Jews are princes
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון holds that every Jew counts as a prince, so all may use rose oil.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: All of ישראל are princes.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון disagrees with the anonymous משנה. He gives every Jew the status of princes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי שמעון, rose oil is never a sign of medicine for a Jew. Since every Jew counts as royalty, using it is considered normal, and it is permitted on שבת.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
All of Israel are princes.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר כׇּל יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּנֵי מְלָכִים הֵם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disputes the rose-oil ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All Jews may smear rose oil on שבת.

steps.title: Does vinegar help teeth or harm them?
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר פפא points out that the משנה implies vinegar helps teeth, but a פסוק in משלי says vinegar harms teeth.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רב אחא the tall one, who is רב אחא בר פפא, raised a contradiction to רבי אבהו: We learned that one with a toothache may not sip vinegar. Does that mean vinegar is good for teeth? But it is written: 'Like vinegar to the teeth and smoke to the eyes'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by setting the משנה against a פסוק. One source suggests vinegar heals teeth, and the other suggests it hurts them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only forbids sipping vinegar because it is healing, which assumes vinegar helps teeth. משלי compares a lazy messenger to vinegar on teeth, which assumes vinegar hurts them.

keyTerms.meaning: גמרא, the discussion of the משנה

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Rav Acha the tall raised a contradiction

phrases.aramaic: דְּהוּא רַב אַחָא בַּר פָּפָּא לְרַבִּי אֲבָהוּ:
phrases.english: (who is Rav Acha bar Pappa) before Rabbi Abbahu:
We learned: One who has pain in his teeth —
may not sip vinegar through them.
Is that to say that vinegar is good for teeth?!
But isn't it written:
'Like vinegar to the teeth and like smoke to the eyes'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes the first case of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's assumption that vinegar heals teeth.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק says vinegar harms teeth.

steps.title: Fruit vinegar versus wine vinegar
steps.stepSummary: First answer: the two sources speak about different kinds of vinegar.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult: this one refers to fruit vinegar, and that one refers to wine vinegar.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by saying each source refers to a different type of vinegar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק that says vinegar harms teeth refers to fruit vinegar. The משנה, which treats vinegar as healing, refers to wine vinegar. So there is no contradiction.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this refers to fruit vinegar,
phrases.notes: This is the vinegar the פסוק is talking about, the harmful kind.

phrases.english: that refers to wine vinegar.
phrases.notes: This is the vinegar the משנה is talking about, the healing kind.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both sources speak about the same vinegar.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק refers to fruit vinegar; the משנה refers to wine vinegar.

steps.title: Wound versus no wound
steps.stepSummary: Second answer: both refer to wine vinegar; it heals when there is a wound but weakens healthy teeth.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or if you want, say both refer to wine vinegar: this is where there is a wound, and that is where there is no wound. Where there is a wound, it heals; where there is no wound, it weakens.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers another answer. It is the same vinegar, but the effect depends on the condition of the teeth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה speaks of a person in pain, who has a wound, so vinegar heals him. The פסוק speaks of healthy teeth, which vinegar weakens.

keyTerms.meaning: and if you wish, say (another answer)

steps.whatToRemember: Vinegar and teeth: either it depends on the kind of vinegar (fruit or wine), or on whether there is a wound (it heals a wound but weakens healthy teeth).

phrases.english: And if you wish, say: both this and that refer to wine vinegar:
this is where there is a wound,
that is where there is no wound.
Where there is a wound — it heals,
where there is no wound — it weakens.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second resolution to the same contradiction.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing two situations (condition of the teeth)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The difference must be in the kind of vinegar.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even wine vinegar heals a wound but weakens healthy teeth.

steps.title: A ברייתא seems to permit sipping vinegar
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule against sipping vinegar for the teeth. It then challenges it with a ברייתא that permits sipping and swallowing.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says one may not sip vinegar through his teeth on שבת. But a ברייתא teaches: one may not sip and spit it out, but one may sip and swallow it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the line from the משנה. It then raises a ברייתא that seems to allow what the משנה forbids.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה sounds like a blanket ban on sipping vinegar for the teeth. The ברייתא splits the case. Spitting it out looks like medicine and is forbidden. Swallowing it looks like normal drinking and is allowed. So which is right?

keyTerms.meaning: sip, draw liquid in through the teeth

steps.confusionAlert: Swallowing is allowed because it looks like ordinary drinking. Spitting is forbidden because it clearly shows the person is treating his teeth. That is the medicine-on-שבת concern.

phrases.english: One may not sip vinegar through them (the teeth).
But wasn't it taught: one may not sip and spit out,
but one may sip and swallow!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the same clause of the משנה already discussed in steps 11–13 (sipping vinegar). This time it raises a new challenge from a ברייתא about whether swallowing is permitted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's apparently total ban on sipping vinegar
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא permits sipping and swallowing, while the משנה seems to forbid all sipping.

steps.title: אביי: the משנה is about spitting out
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the משנה only forbids sipping and spitting out.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: When we learned the משנה, we learned it about one who sips and spits out.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the contradiction. He reads the משנה as talking only about the spitting case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the משנה is limited to spitting, it fully agrees with the ברייתא. Both forbid spitting, and swallowing stays permitted.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
When we learned our Mishnah as well,
we learned it about one who sips and spits out.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר אַבָּיֵי: כִּי תְּנַן נָמֵי מַתְנִיתִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה forbids all sipping, even swallowing.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה forbids only sipping and spitting out.

steps.title: רבא: before dipping versus after dipping
steps.stepSummary: רבא says that even swallowing can be forbidden. The ברייתא permits it before dipping food; the משנה forbids it after dipping.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Even if you say the משנה is about sipping and swallowing, here it is before dipping and there it is after dipping.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different answer. He keeps the משנה as covering swallowing too and divides the cases by timing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before a person dips his food in the vinegar, sipping it looks like normal enjoyment, so it is allowed. After the meal's dipping is done, there is no food reason to drink vinegar, so it clearly looks like medicine and is forbidden.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Even if you say it is about sipping and swallowing,
here — before dipping,
here — after dipping.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא מְגַמֵּעַ וּבוֹלֵעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to the same קשיא, different from אביי's.
steps.terutzMaskana: Swallowing is permitted before dipping and forbidden after dipping.

steps.title: Challenge to רבא from his own principle of הוֹאִיל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: since sipping before dipping is allowed, it should also be allowed after dipping, because רבא accepts the principle of הוֹאִיל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say: since before dipping it is permitted, after dipping it is also permitted! For we heard that רבא holds of 'since' (הוֹאִיל).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא's answer with a rule that רבא himself holds. This step sets up the proof in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: הוֹאִיל means: since something is allowed in one situation, we allow it in a similar situation too and don't create a split. If רבא holds this, then permission before dipping should carry over to after dipping, and his distinction falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: and let us say (introduces a challenge)
'since', the principle that a permission in one case extends to a parallel case
for we heard of him (that he holds)

phrases.english: And let us say: since before dipping it is permitted —
after dipping it is also permitted.
For we have heard of Rava
that he holds of 'since.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבא's distinction from step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's split between before dipping and after dipping
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבא's own הוֹאִיל principle should erase that split.

steps.title: Proof that רבא holds הוֹאִיל: שבת and יום הכפורים
steps.stepSummary: רבא said that nothing is permitted on שבת yet forbidden on יום הכפורים. Since something is permitted on שבת, it is permitted on יום הכפורים too.
steps.simpleTranslation: For רבא said: There is nothing that is permitted on שבת and forbidden on יום הכפורים. Since it is permitted on שבת, it is also permitted on יום הכפורים!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves that רבא holds of הוֹאִיל by quoting his statement about שבת and יום הכפורים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is טבילה (immersion). On שבת it is allowed because it looks like cooling off for pleasure. On יום הכפורים pleasure-bathing is forbidden, so that reason doesn't apply. Yet רבא still permits it there, simply because it is permitted on שבת. That is הוֹאִיל in action.

phrases.english: For Rava said:
There is nothing that is permitted on Shabbat
and forbidden on Yom Kippur;
since it is permitted on Shabbat —
on Yom Kippur it is also permitted!

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רָבָא: לֵיכָּא מִידֵּי דִּבְשַׁבָּת שְׁרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the claim in step 17.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבא's statement equating שבת and יום הכפורים regarding טבילה

steps.title: רבא retracted one of his positions
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבא retracted 'this', meaning his before/after dipping distinction.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא retracted from this one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the conflict by saying רבא changed his mind about one of his two statements.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's two statements can't both stand: the dipping split clashes with הוֹאִיל. So one of them was dropped. Here 'this' points to the vinegar distinction, which means the explanation of the משנה would go back to אביי's approach.

phrases.english: Rava retracted from this one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of steps 17–18.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבא held both the dipping distinction and הוֹאִיל.

steps.title: How do we know which statement he retracted?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we know רבא retracted the vinegar distinction. Maybe he retracted the יום הכפורים ruling instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know he retracted from this one? Perhaps he retracted from that one!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the answer it just gave. It asks which of רבא's two statements was actually dropped. This sets up the proof in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Either statement could have been dropped to remove the clash. If רבא gave up the יום הכפורים ruling (and with it הוֹאִיל), his vinegar distinction could still stand.

phrases.english: From where do we know that he retracted from this one?
Perhaps he retracted from that one?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the retraction answer of step 19.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which of רבא's two statements did he retract?

steps.title: A ברייתא supports the יום הכפורים ruling
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that everyone obligated to immerse does so as usual, even on תשעה באב and יום הכפורים. So רבא would not have retracted that ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: It cannot enter your mind, for it was taught: All who are obligated in immersions immerse in their usual way, both on תשעה באב and on יום הכפורים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves that רבא could not have dropped his יום הכפורים ruling, because a ברייתא states the same thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since a ברייתא permits טבילה on יום הכפורים, רבא's ruling there has firm backing, and he would not abandon it. So the statement he retracted must be the vinegar distinction between before and after dipping.

keyTerms.meaning: it cannot enter your mind (rejecting a suggestion)

steps.whatToRemember: רבא kept his הוֹאִיל ruling about טבילה on יום הכפורים, which a ברייתא supports. He dropped his before/after dipping split, so the vinegar question goes back to אביי's answer: only sipping and spitting out is forbidden.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that a person may immerse as usual on יום הכפורים and תשעה באב. It also shows how the גמרא decides which of a sage's statements he retracted: the one with outside support stays.

phrases.english: It cannot enter your mind,
for it was taught: All who are obligated in immersions
immerse in their usual manner,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין בְּתִשְׁעָה בְּאָב בֵּין בְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים.
phrases.english: both on the Ninth of Av and on Yom Kippur.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ, דְּתַנְיָא: כׇּל חַיָּיבֵי טְבִילוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the שאלה of step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The יום הכפורים ruling is backed by a ברייתא, so the retraction must be from the vinegar distinction.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבא retracted his before/after dipping distinction. Immersion as usual on יום הכפורים remains permitted.

steps.title: רב rules like רבי שמעון on rose oil
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about pain in the loins. רבי אבא בר זבדא reports in the name of רב that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'One who has pain in his loins, etc.' רבי אבא בר זבדא said in the name of רב: The הלכה follows רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new part of the משנה, about someone with pain in his loins. It gives רב's ruling that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון, who permits rubbing rose oil on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the תנא קמא says only princes may rub rose oil on their wounds, because princes use it on weekdays too. Ordinary people may not, because for them it is clearly medicine. רבי שמעון says all Jews are like princes, so everyone may use it, and רב rules like him.

keyTerms.meaning: One who has pain in his loins (lower back and hips)
'Etc.' The rest of the משנה is assumed, not quoted
The practical law follows the opinion of…
Rose oil, an expensive oil normally used by princes

steps.whyThisMatters: This ruling becomes the target of the next challenge. The גמרא will ask whether it fits with other things רב said.

phrases.english: 'One who has pain in his loins, etc.'
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה. Rose oil is forbidden for ordinary people, and רבי שמעון permits it.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר זַבְדָּא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rabbi Abba bar Zavda said that Rav said:
The halakha follows Rabbi Shimon.
phrases.notes: So everyone may rub rose oil on his loins on שבת.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר זַבְדָּא אָמַר רַב הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic. The earlier discussion about רבא, vinegar, and יום הכפורים has ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רב, the הלכה follows רבי שמעון: anyone may rub rose oil on aching loins on שבת.

steps.title: Does רב really follow רבי שמעון?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא is surprised that רב would rule like רבי שמעון. It begins to quote a teaching of רב, reported by רב שימי בר חייא, about a cloth stopper in a barrel spout. That teaching seems to show that רב does not follow רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this mean that רב holds like רבי שמעון? But didn't רב שימי בר חייא say in the name of רב: this cloth stopper of a barrel…
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ruling it just quoted. It begins to bring a different statement of רב that seems to contradict it. The quote is not finished yet, so the full challenge comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'is that to say' shows surprise: the גמרא knows of another ruling by רב that seems to go against רבי שמעון. That ruling is about a cloth stopper pushed into a barrel's spout on שבת. If רב rules against רבי שמעון there, it is hard to see why he would rule like him here.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Is that to say…?' A phrase of surprise that opens a challenge
'But didn't he say…?' It brings a contradicting statement
A cloth stopper, a rag used to plug an opening

steps.confusionAlert: The sentence stops in the middle. Do not try to finish the challenge yet. רב's ruling about the stopper, and why it contradicts רבי שמעון, comes on the next amud.

phrases.aramaic: לְמֵימְרָא דְּרַב כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן סְבִירָא לֵיהּ?
phrases.english: Is that to say that Rav holds like Rabbi Shimon?
phrases.notes: The גמרא is surprised here and is about to point out a contradiction.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָאָמַר רַב שִׁימִי בַּר חִיָּיא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב:
phrases.english: But didn't Rav Shimi bar Ḥiyya say in the name of Rav:
This cloth stopper of a barrel…
phrases.notes: The teaching continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמֵימְרָא דְּרַב כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן סְבִירָא לֵיהּ וְהָאָמַר רַב שִׁימִי בַּר חִיָּיא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב's ruling from step 22 by pointing to another ruling of רב.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון about rose oil.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another teaching of רב, about a cloth stopper in a barrel spout, seems to go against רבי שמעון. That makes it unlikely that רב follows רבי שמעון here. The details are given on the next amud.
